==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈlæŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|a=RP,AU}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈlaŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|a=SSB,Northern England,Scotland,Wales}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈlæŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|/ˈleɪŋ-/|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈlæŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|[ˈlæŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ]|a=NYC,New Orleans,Philadelphia,Baltimore}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈlæŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|[ˈlæŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ]|~|[ˈlæə̯ŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ]|~|[ˈlɛə̯ŋ-]|a=Southern US}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈlæŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|[ˈlɛə̯ŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ]|a=Inland North}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈleɪŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|[ˈleɪ̯ŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ]|~|[ˈleːŋ-]|a=[[w:North-Central American English|North-Central US]]}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈleɪŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ/|/ˈlæŋ-/|;|[ˈleɪŋ.ɡwɪd͡ʒ]|~|[ˈlɛːŋ-]|~|[ˈlæŋ-]|a=Western US,Midland US,Western Pennsylvania,New England}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-language.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈlɛŋ.ɡwəd͡ʒ/|a=NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈlæŋɡ.weːd͡ʒ/|a=India}} * {{rhymes|en|æŋɡwɪdʒ|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|lan|guage}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:langage|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|langage}}, {{m|enm|language}}, from {{der|en|fro|language}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*linguāticum}}, from {{der|en|la|lingua||tongue, speech, language}}, from {{der|en|itc-ola|dingua||tongue}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s||tongue, speech, language}}. {{doublet|en|langaj}}. {{displaced|ang|ġeþēode}}. Mostly, but not fully, displaced native {{cog|en|tongue}}, in this specific sense, in common as well as academic usage. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} {{examples| The English Wiktionary uses the English '''language''' to define words from all of the world's '''languages'''.

[[File:Hello1.ogv|200px]]
This person is saying "hello" in American Sign '''Language'''. }} {{wp}} # {{senseid|en|Q315}}{{lb|en|countable}} A [[body]] of [[word]]s, and set of methods of combining them (called a [[grammar]]), understood by a [[community]] and used as a form of [[communication]]. #: {{ux|en|The English and German '''languages''' are both members of the West Germanic '''language''' family.}} #: {{ux|en|Deaf and mute people communicate using sign '''language'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|page=50|year=1900|author={{w|William Thomas Beckford|William Beckford}}| title=[http://books.google.com/books?id=KnArAAAAMAAJ The History of the Caliph Vathek]| passage=No '''language''' could express his rage and despair.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=John Malathronas|title=Which languages are easiest – and most difficult – for native English speakers to learn?|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/learn-a-foreign-language-wellness|date=2021-04-25|passage=Many of us have entertained the idea of expanding our horizons. Learning a foreign '''language''' is an obvious option.
It’s one that I would personally endorse: My individual circumstances were such that, by the age of 12, I could speak German, Greek and English, so '''languages''' became my passion and my hobby.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220322023413/https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/learn-a-foreign-language-wellness}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} The ability to communicate using words. #: {{ux|en|the gift of '''language'''}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1805|month=December|author=Julius Griffiths|title=A Journey across the Desert|journal=The Monthly Mirror|page=362 |passage=It is wholly out of the power of '''language''' to convey any idea of the blissful enjoyment of obtaining water, after an almost total want of it, during eight and forty hours, in the scorching regions of an Arabian desert, in the month of July.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} A [[sublanguage]]: the [[slang]] of a [[particular]] [[community]] or [[jargon]] of a [[particular]] [[specialist]] [[field]]. #: {{ux|en|legal '''language''';   the '''language''' of chemistry}} #* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|chapter=Prologue|passage=Thus, when he drew up instructions in lawyer '''language''', he expressed the important words by an initial, a medial, or a final consonant, and made scratches for all the words between; his clerks, however, understood him very well.}} #* {{RQ:Fry Liar|page=24|passage=And ‘[[blub]]bing’ . . . [[blub|Blub]]bing went out with ‘decent’ and ‘ripping’. Mind you, not a bad new '''language''' to start up. 1920s schoolboy slang could be due for a revival.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:CBC Radio|title=Take more selfies! Curator wants Indigenous people to flood social media with their photos|date=January 11 2019|quotee=Sherry Farrell Racette |text="The '''language''' of photography — load, shoot, aim — it's the '''language''' of guns," she said. "They were in the sights of the camera, the same way that they were also within the sights of a gun." |url=https://www.cbc.ca/radio/unreserved/iconic-indigenous-imagery-how-photos-shape-movements-and-connect-us-to-history-1.4963770/take-more-selfies-curator-wants-indigenous-people-to-flood-social-media-with-their-photos-1.4971621 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250825060010/https://www.cbc.ca/radio/unreserved/iconic-indigenous-imagery-how-photos-shape-movements-and-connect-us-to-history-1.4963770/take-more-selfies-curator-wants-indigenous-people-to-flood-social-media-with-their-photos-1.4971621}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} The specific wording or style of a text, such as a law or a contract. #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Peter Ludlow|authorlink=Peter Ludlow|title=The Living Word|url=https://archive.nytimes.com/opinionator.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/04/22/the-living-word/|date=2012-04-22|accessdate=2026-01-23|text=Technological advances are notorious for exposing the open-endedness of the '''language''' in our laws, even when we thought our definitions were airtight. Lawmakers can’t anticipate everything. Indeed, you could make the case that the whole area of patent law just is the problem of deciding whether some new technology should fall within the range of the '''language''' of the patent.}} # {{lb|en|countable|uncountable|figurative}} The expression of thought (the communication of meaning) in a specified way; that which communicates something, as language does. #: {{ux|en|body '''language''';   the '''language''' of the eyes}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=Eugene C. Kennedy; Sara C. Charles|title=On Becoming a Counselor|isbn=0824519132 |passage=A tale about themselves [is] told by people with help from the universal '''languages''' of their eyes, their hands, and even their shirting feet.}} # {{lb|en|countable|uncountable}} A [[body]] of [[sound]]s, [[sign]]s or [[signal]]s by which [[animal]]s [[communicate]], and by which [[plant]]s are sometimes also [[thought]] to [[communicate]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1983|title=The Listener|volume=110|page=14 |passage=A more likely hypothesis was that the attacked leaves were transmitting some airborne chemical signal to sound the alarm, rather like insects sending out warnings {{...}} But this is the first time that a plant-to-plant '''language''' has been detected.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|title=Animals in Translation|page=274 |passage=Prairie dogs use their '''language''' to refer to real dangers in the real world, so it definitely has meaning.}} # {{lb|en|computing|countable}} A [[computer language]]; a [[machine language]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Kent D. Lee|title=Foundations of Programming Languages|isbn=3319133144|page=94 |passage=In fact pointers are called references in these '''languages''' to distinguish them from pointers in '''languages''' like C and C++.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} A [[manner]] of [[expression]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1782|author=William Cowper|title=Hope|text=Their '''language''' simple, as their manners meek, {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} The particular words used in a [[speech]] or a [[passage]] of [[text]]. #: {{ux|en|The '''language''' used in the law does not permit any other interpretation.}} #:
